title: Sheet-return local operators and their weight filtrations
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $m\ge1$, $k_m=\mathbf F_{q^m}\subset k$, $X_{0,m}=X_0\times_{k_0}k_m$, and $Y=X_{0,m}\times_{k_0}k$. Use the actual common-stage coefficient categories, constructible hearts and Weil sheaves of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], [def-weil-constructible-heart] and [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], and the integral-normalized pullback comparisons of [def-zl-weil-ind-sheaf-category]. Write $g_X$ for geometric $q$-Frobenius on $X$, $H$ for geometric $q$-Frobenius on $Y$, and $P=Lg_X^*$ on the constructible heart [def-weil-frobenius-detailed].

Let $(N,\eta)$ be any constructible $k_0$-Weil sheaf on $X_{0,m}$. Define its sheet return $R(N,\eta)=(j_0^*N,\phi)$ over $k_m$, where $j_0:X\to Y$ is the distinguished sheet and $\phi:L(g_X^m)^*j_0^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}j_0^*N$ is the composite of the $m$ successive pullbacks of $\eta$, using $H^m j_0=j_0g_X^m$ and the specified compositors. For every closed point $z\in X_{0,m}$, put $r=[\kappa(z):k_m]$. The local operators of $(N,\eta)$ in its $k_0$ interpretation and of $R(N,\eta)$ in its $k_m$ interpretation are conjugate, and both absolute residue sizes are $q^{mr}=\#\kappa(z)$.

More precisely, with compatible geometric points on the distinguished sheet, the canonical stalk identification intertwines the two operators defined by exactly the iterated point transports of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]: the $r$ return transitions for $H^m$ give the same ordered $mr$ factors and the same point transport as the $mr$ transitions for $H$. This identification holds at finite coefficients and on whole integral coefficient towers with their specified derived-limit realization, and then after rationalization and at common-stage $\Qlb$ coefficients. It is natural in Weil morphisms and compatible with finite coefficient extension. Changing the residue embedding or geometric point changes the stalk identification by conjugacy. No lissity, semisimplicity or finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis is imposed.

Fix $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$. With punctual purity and mixed filtrations as in [def-weil-punctual-weights], a sheaf and its sheet return are punctually pure of weight $w$ simultaneously for every real $w$. On a morphism $u$ of constructible $k_0$-Weil sheaves put $R(u)=j_0^*u$; this makes $R$ an exact functor to constructible $k_m$-Weil sheaves on $X_{0,m}$. For every finite filtration of $(N,\eta)$ by constructible $k_0$-Weil subsheaves, the filtration of $R(N,\eta)$ by the sheet returns of its terms has quotients $R(N_r)/R(N_{r-1})\simeq R(N_r/N_{r-1})$, punctually pure of exactly the same specified weights as the corresponding quotients of the original filtration. Conversely, for every finite filtration of $R(N,\eta)$ by constructible $k_m$-Weil subsheaves there is a unique finite filtration of $(N,\eta)$ by constructible $k_0$-Weil subsheaves whose sheet returns are, as subobjects of $R(N,\eta)$, the given terms, and its quotients are punctually pure of the same weights as the corresponding given quotients. This includes arbitrary upper weight bounds, zero stalks and the empty scheme.

source.place: (1.1.7)--(1.1.10), pp. 150--152, and (1.2.6), p. 154; ordered block and finite-filtration consequences.

proof.text: Apply the common-stage local spectra statement using the rational operator and scalar clauses. This supplies the residue-degree, residue-cardinality and local conjugacy conclusions. Unfold punctual purity: replace its eigenvalue predicate by the equivalent predicate at every closed point. Both schemes have definitionally the same residue fields, so the absolute-value equations and every specified real weight agree.

source.place: (1.1.7)--(1.1.10), pp. 150--152, and (1.2.6), p. 154; ordered block and finite-filtration consequences.

proof.text: For each N, lower MonoOver.congr of the return equivalence to the thin skeleton and take its order isomorphism. Its image of U is mk(R.map U.arrow). Preservation of cokernels and the canonical underlying isomorphisms of subobject representatives identify all quotient objects. Apply the proved purity equivalence to each quotient, transporting along this isomorphism. OrderIso.arrowCongr gives the finite-chain equivalence. Injectivity and preservation of bottom and top give the endpoint equations, also for length zero.

source.place: (1.1.7)--(1.1.10), pp. 150--152, and (1.2.6), p. 154; ordered block and finite-filtration consequences.

proof.text: Map a finite mixed filtration through R: exactness preserves zero objects, monomorphisms and cokernels, and the purity comparison preserves each quotient weight and its upper bound. Conversely map the filtration through the inverse equivalence. The counit transports purity back to every inverse image, and the unit identifies the final inverse image with N. This proves both implications using the actual finite-object-and-monomorphism definition of mixedness.
